1.  The series

The tebako ecosystem packages applications and runtimes into single executables whose loading behavior is governed by normative specifications: the wire format of the package container, the manifest grammar of a payload, the contract between the loader and a runtime, and the policies for resolution, caching, jailing, trust, and observability. Those normative texts live as Markdown files in the product repository, and an implementer — a runtime factory author, a registry operator, a feedstock maintainer — has until now read them only as raw Markdown source, with no rendered document to cite.

The Tebako Specifications (TBK SPEC) series closes that gap. Each document in the series is one normative text from the repository, converted to a Metanorma standard document and rendered to HTML and PDF as a member of a single collection. The document numbering follows the numbering of the source files: TBK SPEC 02 renders 02-tpkg-wire-format.md, and so on. Section numbering, section titles, tables, and code listings are carried over verbatim, so a reference of the form "spec 06 §4" resolves identically against the Markdown source and against the rendered document.

2.  Source of truth and synchronization

The Markdown files under docs/spec/ in the tamatebako/tebako repository are the source of truth for every document in the series. This series is their rendered form; the AsciiDoc twin of a specification is derived from the Markdown and never edited independently. The Markdown sources themselves are not modified by the rendering process.

Each rendered document records the blob SHA of the Markdown file it was converted from in a comment line of the form // source: docs/spec/NN-name.md @ <sha>. The drift gate at docs/spec-site/tools/sync.rb recomputes the blob SHA of every referenced Markdown source and compares it with the recorded value. The gate exits with status 0 when every rendered twin is current, and exits 1 naming the drifted documents when a Markdown source has moved without its rendered twin being updated. A continuous-integration job runs the gate on every pull request that touches docs/spec/, so a specification edit cannot land without its rendered twin following it.

The conversion from Markdown to AsciiDoc is performed and reviewed by hand; the gate does not regenerate document content. After a specification edit has been carried into its twin and reviewed, ruby docs/spec-site/tools/sync.rb --sync updates the recorded SHAs to bless the new state.
